title: Why synthetic media is a new kind of cybersecurity threat
gist: Reality Defender's CEO argues synthetic media is a cybersecurity threat to shared reality, with generation outpacing verification and the 'liar's dividend' eroding trust; he proposes a six-pillar trust infrastructure of authentication, detection, provenance, platform escalation, crisis protocols and governance.

insights.claim: Synthetic media attacks the shared reality institutions use to make decisions rather than systems or data, and content generation is becoming faster and cheaper while verification stays fragmented and slow.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Verification latency is the vulnerability; demand for real-time detection and authentication tools.
insights.locator: A new kind of cybersecurity problem

insights.claim: A fabricated military, election or emergency message can move markets, trigger protests or alter military calculations before specialists prove it false.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Deepfake event risk for markets and geopolitical flashpoints.

insights.claim: The 'liar's dividend' lets bad actors both manufacture evidence and dismiss genuine evidence as fake, and a 2026 audio study found people increasingly distrusted authentic speech without better spotting synthetic speech.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: The larger harm is general distrust, not just belief in fakes.

insights.claim: Trust in news fell in 29 of 48 markets in the Reuters Institute's 2026 Digital News Report, reaching a record-low global trust of 37%.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum

insights.claim: During the 2026 US midterm cycle political organizations released realistic AI-generated videos of candidates, and Brazil's electoral court set binding standards on synthetic depictions of political figures.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Regulatory and election-integrity pressure is rising.

insights.claim: The proposed layered trust infrastructure has six pillars: authentication (signatures, verifiable credentials, C2PA), real-time multimodal detection, provenance, platform escalation channels, crisis response protocols and enforceable governance such as EU AI Act transparency rules.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Map of the product and policy categories likely to grow around deepfake defense.

insights.claim: Provenance such as SynthID or C2PA metadata cannot alone authenticate unsigned or anonymous uploads because bad actors can strip or omit metadata.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Provenance is necessary but insufficient; detection still needed.

insights.claim: The goal is not to eliminate synthetic media but to preserve the ability to tell evidence from fabrication when consequences are greatest, with the next era of cybersecurity protecting confidence in reality itself.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
